highlights: Mistral AI released the weights of Le Chonk, an improved Mistral Large 4 with stronger reasoning efficiency, while Liquid AI introduced the 2.2B-parameter LFM3-Omni-2B for on-device multimodal work and Recursive published the Apache 2.0 Flint coding-agent model.

New benchmarks for computer-use and CLI agents expose large collaboration gaps: PersonaCUABench found mean task completion fell by 36% for persona requests, and REALCLI's best configuration scored only 49.2% on average.
Developer tooling moved fast, with Claude Code v2.1.314, Codex 0.166.0, and a Hugging Face Transformers patch release v5.21.1 shipping new permissions, diagnostics, and bug fixes.

items.title: Mistral AI releases Le Chonk weights for Mistral Large 4
items.summary: Mistral AI has released the weights of Le Chonk, an improved Mistral Large 4 that the company says brings substantial gains in reasoning efficiency and lower inference costs. The model is a 1-trillion-parameter, natively multimodal mixture-of-experts design with 49 billion active parameters per token and a 1M context length, giving developers an open-weight option for coding and agentic workloads.

evidence.quote: We release the weights of Le Chonk, advancing the frontier of open models in agentic coding and cybersecurity.
Earlier this month, we released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), our flagship 1-trillion-parameter, natively multimodal model, in public preview.
Today, we're releasing the weights of this improved Mistral Large 4.
The new model also features substantial gains in reasoning efficiency that give developers greater performance while lowering inference costs.
Mistral Large 4 ranks as the best open-weight model for coding and among the world's most capable open models overall.

Trained from scratch on European infrastructure with clear lineage from inception to release, it gives organizations a trusted foundation for Sovereign AI Mistral is defining the sovereign AI category and leading the open frontier.
We're committed to building the world's most capable models and releasing them openly, giving developers, enterprises, and institutions the power to own, customize, and control their AI.
On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Mistral Large 4 improved by 13 percentage points to 41% compared to its public preview, taking the lead among open-weight models while reducing output tokens by 30%.

ree reasoning modes: Mode Recommended Use Low Simple tasks; replaces ‘None’ reasoning mode Medium Everyday tasks High (default) Hardest use cases requiring high precision and thorough reasoning Beyond benchmarks, Mistral Large 4's coding capabilities are validated by human preference.

Mistral Large 4 scores 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, which measures a model’s ability to discover vulnerabilities in a codebase, reproduce and validate them, and patch them without breaking existing functionality.
Our model’s built-in guardrails distinguishes between defensive and malicious, offensive cybersecurity tasks.

items.title: Liquid AI ships LFM3-Omni-2B for on-device multimodal tasks
items.summary: LFM3-Omni-2B is Liquid AI's first omni-modal model in the LFM3 family, a single end-to-end model that understands text, images, video and audio and answers in text and speech. At 2.2B parameters, it is designed to run efficiently on phones, laptops and other edge hardware, replacing a separate ASR model, vision-language model, LLM and TTS model.

evidence.quote: LFM3-Omni-2B is Liquid AI 's first omni-modal model in the LFM3 family: a single end-to-end model that understands text, images, video and audio , and answers in text and speech .
It is built for on-device use: one model replaces a separate ASR model, vision-language model, LLM and TTS model.
Any input, text or speech output: ask about a photo by voice, transcribe or translate speech, chat out loud, or ask questions about a video and its soundtrack together.
Watches and listens together: for videos with sound, the model sees and hears them at the same time, so it can answer questions that need both.
Small enough for devices: at 2.2B parameters, it is designed to run efficiently on phones, laptops and other edge hardware.
Find more information about the LFM3 family in our release blog post .

items.title: Recursive releases Flint, a mixture-of-experts model for coding agents
items.summary: Flint is Recursive's mixture-of-experts language model for coding agents, with 39.8 billion total parameters and approximately 2.5 billion active per token. It supports text input and output, reasoning and multi-turn tool use, and the Apache 2.0 release includes the BF16 checkpoint, tokenizer, chat template and an SGLang serving kit.

evidence.quote: Flint is Recursive’s mixture-of-experts language model for coding agents, with 39.8 billion total parameters and approximately 2.5 billion active per token.
It is designed to investigate codebases, fix bugs, implement features, and write tests.
Flint supports text input and output, reasoning, and multi-turn tool use.
In our release evaluations, it scores 54.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 89.7% on SWE-bench Pro v2, and 74.2% on SWE-bench Verified.
This repository contains the BF16 checkpoint, model configuration, tokenizer, chat template, and an SGLang serving kit.
Quantized variants are prepared separately for NVIDIA and Apple Silicon runtimes.
Flint runs on one B300 or H200 GPU per replica with the SGLang kit in sglang/ .
Flint is released under the Apache 2.0 license .

items.title: OpenAI updates its Model Spec and explains misalignment detection
items.summary: OpenAI's updated Model Spec outlines five core values to guide more capable AI toward sound judgment, human agency and faithfulness to human intent. OpenAI also describes how layered monitoring detects frontier model misalignment and unauthorized agent behavior so responders can intervene before incidents escalate.

items.title: Falcon brings lightweight causal audio-visual speaker extraction
items.summary: Falcon is a causal audio-visual target speaker extraction method paired with the new RealSSA benchmark, whose simulated scenes include 1--5 dynamic near-field interfering speakers. Compared with the causal AV-TFGridNet baseline, Falcon cuts parameters by 91.9%, computation by 20.2 times and GPU inference latency by 11.1 times, with code and a demo available.

evidence.quote: g Huang , Xiaolin Hu Abstract Falcon is a lightweight causal audio-visual target speaker extraction method that achieves high quality with drastically reduced parameters and latency, supported by the realistic RealSSA benchmark.
To address the first gap, we release RealSSA , a realistic AVTSE benchmark consisting of RealSSA -Sim and RealSSA -Real.
RealSSA -Sim provides controllable simulated scenes with 1--5 dynamic near-field interfering speakers; scenes with far-field interference additionally include 10--15 far-field interfering speakers.
RealSSA -Real provides a held-out real-recorded evaluation set.
To address the second gap, we propose Falcon , a causal AVTSE method.
Its Separator performs multi-scale time-frequency separation in a single encoder--decoder pass.
We train Falcon with an encoder-space speaker contrastive loss .
This loss suppresses near-field leakage at zero inference cost and transfers across backbones.
Falcon achieves state-of-the-art extraction quality on RealSSA -Sim, LRS2-2Mix, LRS3-2Mix, and VoxCeleb2-2Mix.
Compared with the causal AV-TFGridNet baseline, it cuts parameters by 91.9%, computation by 20.2 times, and GPU inference latency by 11.1 times.
Code and demo are available at https://cslikai.cn/ Falcon /.

items.title: Baidu releases Unlimited-OCR-2 for unlimited-horizon document parsing
items.summary: Unlimited OCR 2 achieves unlimited-horizon parsing with Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA), which compresses text-visual attention from ultra-long sequences into a fixed-size set of working references such as 512 tokens. The release supports Transformers for quick tests and SGLang for serving, and the authors report state-of-the-art results on both dozens-of-pages and hundred-page document benchmarks.

evidence.quote: [2026/10/27] 📊 We release MarathonDocBench , a new benchmark for ultra-long document parsing.
[2026/10/27] 🚀 We release Unlimited OCR 2 , achieving unlimited-horizon parsing with SR-SWA.
What's New in 2
Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA): Compresses text-visual attention interactions from ultra-long sequences down to a fixed-size set of working references (e.g., 512 tokens).
This bounds computational complexity, keeping per-step decoding latency and memory footprint nearly constant regardless of document length.

From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing: Powered by SR-SWA, Unlimited-OCR 2 achieves true, unbounded document parsing within a finite context window—effectively eliminating quadratic attention scaling and memory bottlenecks as documents grow.
Ultra-Long Document Parsing SOTA: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across both dozens-of-pages benchmarks (e.g., MPDocBench) and extreme hundred-page benchmarks (e.g., MarathonDocBench).
Unlimited OCR 2 supports Transformers (native, for quick tests) and SGLang (recommended for serving).

items.title: IBM updates Granite Switch 4.1.1 with a new ASR model
items.summary: Granite Switch 4.1.1 is a patch release that is fully backwards compatible with 4.1, requiring no migration, with incremental improvements under the hood. It updates the Granite Speech ASR model for multilingual speech-to-text across 10 languages with native punctuation and capitalization, and updates the Decision adapter in granitelib-core without recomputing the base model.

evidence.quote: Just over a week ago, we released Granite Switch 4.1 , showing that our modular Switch architecture lets you configure a language model with specialized, cache-efficient adapters — adding new expertise on a single endpoint.
Granite Switch 4.1.1 is a patch release.
The version number means what it means in software: fully backwards compatible with 4.1, no migration, incremental improvements under the hood.

Updated Granite Speech ASR model — multilingual speech-to-text across 10 languages with native punctuation and capitalization, so transcripts are ready for downstream models without a formatting pass.
Updated Decision adapter in granitelib-core — featuring improved overall performance on the Jev Decision Index test set.
Apart from training the new ASR model and Decision adapter, nothing was recomputed: the base model is untouched.
You compose the latest adapters you want and deploy.

items.title: TAO jointly schedules LLM agent sessions and tool calls
items.summary: TAO is a tool-aware joint scheduling framework for LLM-based agentic serving that combines near-term tool readiness, node-specific cache credit with time-aware decay and token footprint, then uses a dynamic program to select and place waiting sessions under capacity constraints. Across the 12 reported model-workload-concurrency settings, TAO reduces latency by up to 26.8%, lowers mean time to first token (TTFT) by up to 36.3% and boosts decode throughput by up to 29.5% against the best evaluated baseline for each metric.

evidence.quote: Papers arxiv:2610.37230 TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving Published on Oct 27 · Submitted by Li shuhuai on Oct 29 · AIOR Upvote 18 +10 Authors: Shuhuai Li , Shengdong Ye , Dongdong Ge , Yinyu Ye , Jianghao Lin Abstract TAO improves scheduling for LLM agent services by co
To bridge this gap, we present TAO, a tool-aware joint scheduling framework for LLM-based agentic serving .

Its value interface combines near-term tool readiness, node-specific cache credit with time-aware decay , and token footprint ; a dynamic program jointly selects and places waiting sessions under capacity constraints.

Across the 12 reported model-workload-concurrency settings, TAO reduces latency by up to 26.8%, reduces mean time to first token (TTFT) by up to 36.3%, and increases decode throughput by up to 29.5% relative to the best evaluated state-of-the-art baseline for each metric.
Joint DP Placement: Replaces greedy per-session routing with an asynchronous dynamic program (under 0.12% runtime overhead) that jointly selects and places waiting sessions under GPU capacity limits.
Tested on DeepSeek-V4 Flash, Qwen3-32B, and GLM-4.7, TAO cuts latency by up to 26.8%, lowers mean TTFT by up to 36.3%, and boosts decode throughput by up to 29.5% over leading baselines.

items.title: Sensorimotor Alignment proxies robot policy success offline
items.summary: Sensorimotor Alignment (S^2) is a training-free offline metric measuring how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion. The metric correlates positively with downstream robot task success across model families and can screen vision-language model (VLM) backbones before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs).

evidence.quote: Papers arxiv:2610.31670 Copy markdown Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success Published on Oct 23 · Submitted by Yunfei Xie on Oct 29 #3 Paper of the day · Rice University Upvote 21 +13 Authors: Yunfei Xie , Howard H.

Qian , Shiyi Lan , Kaiyu Hang , Chen Wei Abstract Sensorimotor alignment measures how sensory representations match physical motion geometry, serving as a low-cost offline predictor of robot model performance.
To test this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment (S^2), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion .
We find that S^2 correlates positively with downstream robot task success across model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation.
S^2 can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs).
Beyond this correlation, S^2 offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs).

With S^2, we extend PRH to robotics and make sensorimotor alignment measurable, offering a low-cost, representation-level view of robot foundation models that closed-loop success rates alone cannot reveal.

items.title: PersonaCUABench tests whether computer-use agents serve users
items.summary: PersonaCUABench keeps 74 tasks across 11 domains fixed and varies only who asks, using a persona agent that rewrites each instruction in the user's own words. Across nine backbones (3,330 runs), mean task completion falls by 36% relative to the original requests, showing that CUAs need evaluation on user requirements and constraints rather than task completion alone.

evidence.quote: We introduce PersonaCUABench , which holds 74 tasks across 11 domains fixed and varies only who asks.

A persona agent , playing one of 44 personas in four groups, rewrites each instruction in that user's own words and answers the CUA's questions, while the CUA sees only the dialogue, never the profile or the original instruction.
Across nine backbones (3,330 runs), mean task completion falls by 36% relative to the original requests.

The losses have two sources: in 59.9% of cells that lose points, the agent engages with what the user asked for and still gets it wrong, and 11.2% are stops the user requested that the checker scores as failures.
Even when a persona request is fully completed, the user gives the top satisfaction rating in only 62.7% of cells, against 84.1% for the original requests.
CUAs should therefore be evaluated not only on task completion but also on whether they meet the requirements and constraints users express.

items.title: REALCLI evaluates task execution and collaboration for CLI agents
items.summary: REALCLI is a paired benchmark that unifies evaluation of task execution and human-agent collaboration quality on realistic CLI tasks, using a five-dimensional framework with 22 sub-dimensions and 51 interaction scenario templates. The best configuration attains an average score of only 49.2%, and peak performance under the joint collaboration score (J_{collab}) reaches merely 37.6%, revealing gaps in steerability, trust calibration and safety boundary management.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we present REALCLI , a paired benchmark that unifies the evaluation of task execution and human-agent collaboration quality on realistic CLI tasks.
To comprehensively measure collaboration, REALCLI builds a five-dimensional framework, operationalized into 22 sub-dimensions and 51 interaction scenario templates.

REALCLI provides two modes for paired comparison: REALCLI -EXEC supplies complete specifications upfront, whereas REALCLI -COLLAB introduces a scripted user that delivers progressive information , corrections, constraint revisions, and authorization decisions.

Evaluations reveal profound capability gaps in frontier agents: the best configuration attains an average score of only 49.2%, and when evaluated by the joint collaboration score (J_{collab}), the peak performance reaches merely 37.6%.
These results show that task effectiveness diverges sharply from collaboration quality, with models consistently struggling in steerability , trust calibration , and safety boundary management .
REALCLI provides a rigorous, reproducible foundation for measuring and advancing collaborative CLI agents .

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.314 adds write guards and idle compaction
items.summary: Claude Code v2.1.314 adds permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories so Write, Edit and NotebookEdit refuse paths outside working directories in every permission mode, plus idle compaction for VS Code and Claude Desktop's Code tab where a 200K+ token conversation left idle is summarized. It also fixes Bedrock sessions with many images failing with "400 Input is too long." and Microsoft Foundry sessions with no deployment for the default Sonnet, Opus or Haiku model.

evidence.quote: Added permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories : Write, Edit and NotebookEdit refuse paths outside the working directories in every permission mode
Added idle compaction to VS Code and Claude Desktop's Code tab: a 200K+ token conversation left idle is summarized, and the summary is used on your next message if the prompt cache has expired
Fixed Bedrock sessions with many images failing every turn and /compact with "400 Input is too long." instead of removing older images and compacting

items.title: claude-mem keeps agent context across sessions
